# Office Software Marketplace

> Independent, hands-researched reviews of office, finance, HR and IT software for small and mid-sized teams. 68 full reviews live here as the canonical version; prices are read on the vendor's page and dated. Last updated 2026-09-26.

AIBuilder Marketplace and its sister sites are run by Daniel Haket, a former banker. Every price is read on the vendor's own page and dated; every review says who should skip the tool. Affiliate links never change a verdict. Six sites, one owner.

## Start here
- [Cost-trap atlas](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/atlas.html): every tool in this niche with its documented pricing traps
- [Price Watch](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/price-watch.html): dated price changes, free-tier cuts and renewal jumps
- [Straight answers](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/answers.html): is it worth it, what does it really cost, what is the catch — per tool
- [Tool finder](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/finder.html): pick a tool in under a minute
- [Deals](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/deals.html): current deals and free trials

- [accessiBe Review (2026): From $59/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/accessibe-review.html): accessiBe: $490 is the first figure a visitor sees. The thing you most need to know about this product is not on its pricing page, it is on the FTC’s.
- [ADP Review (2026): No Public Price, Quote Only](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/adp-review.html): ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site. The quote-only posture is normal in payroll.
- [Airia Review (2026): Real Deployments Land in Custom Quotes](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/airia-review.html): Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. As of 20 August 2026 that is over.

- [Arbor Review (2026): Free for Households, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/arbor-review.html): Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s. The honest catches: it only exists in deregulated US states.
- [BackupMaster Review (2026): From $19/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/backupmaster-review.html): BackupMaster: Essentials $19 a month or $205.20 a year, a 10% saving, covers stores up to 300 orders a month. The listing header says free to install.
- [Bill.com Review (2026): From $49/user Plus Per-Payment Fees](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bill-com-review.html): Bill.com: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise - the same four cards as on 15 August 2026.
- [BillingNow Review (2026): $9.99/mo Flat, Three-Day Trial](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/billingnow-review.html): BillingNow: $9.99 a month, or $99.90 a year which the page itself works out to $8.33 a month and labels 'Save 17%'. The pricing is genuinely refreshin
- [Bitvavo Review (2026): MiCA-Regulated, 0.25% Taker Fee](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bitvavo-review.html): Bitvavo — Above that: 0.03%/0.12% from €2,500,000, 0.01%/0.10% from €5,000,000. The honest caveats are crypto-wide, not Bitvavo-specific.
- [Blinq Review (2026): Free Tier, Then $9.99/mo](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/blinq-review.html): Blinq: Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). The core product is honestly cheap.
- [Bolt Business Review (2026): Pricing Not Public, Quote Only](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bolt-business-review.html): Bolt Business: One line the marketing does not carry. The honest boundary is geography: Bolt's network is Europe/Africa-centric across 600+ cities.
- [BookX Review (2026): From $9.99/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bookx-review.html): BookX: Growth is $19.99 or $203.99 a year (15%) for ten locations and team members. The free plan is a demonstration rather than a plan.
- [BugHerd Review (2026): From $42/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bugherd-review.html): BugHerd: Standard about $42/mo (5 members), Studio ~$67/mo (10), Premium ~$125/mo (25). The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly.
- [Bybit Review (2026): 0.1% Per Trade, No Subscription](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bybit-review.html): Bybit — At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker. Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways.
- [Carbon6 Review (2026): From $97/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/carbon6-review.html): Carbon6: What we can verify on the vendor’s own pages today (re-checked 26 Aug 2026). The honest headline here is not pricing but ownership.
- [ChemiCloud Review (2026): From $1.95/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/chemicloud-review.html): ChemiCloud: Shared hosting starts at $1.95/mo on the September campaign. The honest catch is the one every budget host shares.
- [Claude Review (2026): Free Tier, Then $17/mo](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/claude-review.html): Claude: Pro is $17/month with the annual discount ($200 billed up front) or $20 billed monthly. The honest catch is usage limits.
- [CloudTask Review (2026): The $299 Deposit Is the Small Part](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/cloudtask-review.html): CloudTask: Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. The $299 is the honest part and also the small part.
- [Cloudways Review (2026): From $14/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/cloudways-review.html): Cloudways: $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan. "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is.
- [Compliancely Review (2026): Only TIN Matching Has a Price](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/compliancely-review.html): Compliancely — The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a

- [Datarails Review (2026): Excel-Native FP&A, Quote Only](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/datarails-review.html): Datarails publishes three plans. You cannot find out what it costs without talking to sales, and the entry plan is smaller than it looks.
- [Deel Review (2026): EOR From $599 Buys Risk, Not Software](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/deel-review.html): Deel: Pricing is per worker and demo-led. Know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not softwa

- [Dext Review (2026): From $25/mo for 250 Documents](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/dext-review.html): Dext — Add-ons are billed separately: AI Assist $10.5 a month until 31 October, Commerce Lite from $7.50 and Vault free for 100MB then from $4.
- [Dify Review (2026): From $59/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/dify-review.html): Dify: Source-available and free of a software fee to self-host. 'Free' self-hosting isn't free — you own the servers, updates and reliability.
- [Digit Review (2026): From $400/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/digit-review.html): Digit: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15. The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling.
- [Disputifier Review (2026): 20% Commission, No Subscription](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/disputifier-review.html): Disputifier: Free to install, with everything billed on use, and unchanged between those two readings. Free to install is doing a lot of work here.
- [DocSend Review (2026): $10 to Share, $150 for a Data Room](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/docsend-review.html): DocSend: Personal is $10 per user a month billed yearly or $15 billed monthly, one user. The cheap plan is not the product people buy DocSend for.
- [doola Review (2026): $297/yr Plus State Fees](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/doola-review.html): doola: State filing fees run $50 to $500 depending on the state. Convenient especially for non-US founders.
- [Dryground AI Review (2026): Consulting, and Nowhere a Price](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/dryground-ai-review.html): Dryground AI: /pricing, /plans, /services, /about and /contact all return 404. The case studies underneath them name no clients.
- [Emergent Review (2026): Pro Costs More Per Credit](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/emergent-review.html): Emergent: Free $0 (10 credits/mo); Standard $20/mo, or $17/mo billed annually, for 100 credits (the page states a $36 annual saving, 15%).

- [Expertise AI Review (2026): Free, Then Straight to $2,000](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/expertise-ai-review.html): Expertise AI — The ladder was rebuilt since our July read: the Growth tier at $500/mo is gone. The honest catch is that there is no middle any more.

- [Foxit Review (2026): Editor+ Now Bundles the E-Signing](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/foxit-review.html): Foxit: PDF Editor+ is $159.99 per user per year or $13.99 per user per month. Foxit's pitch is being the honest fraction of Acrobat's price.
- [FreshBooks Review (2026): $2.30 Is a Three-Month Rate](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/freshbooks-review.html): FreshBooks: $62.10 on Lite, $116.10 on Plus, $189.00 on Premium. The meter is billable clients, not invoices or revenue: Lite stops at five.
- [Freshservice Review (2026): The ITSM Features Are at Pro](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/freshservice-review.html): Freshservice: Starter $19/agent/mo billed annually or $29 monthly. Price the tier that contains your must-haves plus realistic AI usage, not the start
- [Glide Review (2026): Two Products, Two Pricing Pages](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/glide-review.html): Glide: The classic spreadsheet-to-app builder still has a genuinely free tier. Glide meters updates, not just seats.
- [Goflow Review (2026): Free Forever, Then $2 an Order](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/goflow-review.html): Goflow Core is free forever at $0/mo with no credit card. Core is free forever but no longer the whole platform.
- [Gusto Review (2026): Base Plus $6 to $22 an Employee](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/gusto-review.html): Gusto: Premium $180 plus $22 per person with a dedicated service advisor and HR experts. The base-plus-per-employee model is transparent but adds up.
- [Heard Review (2026): From $129/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/heard-review.html): Heard: Lite $129/mo or $1,548 a year, Essential $169/mo or $2,028, Premium $255/mo or $3,060. Mind the fine print between tiers.
- [Hostinger Review (2026): From $2.99/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/hostinger-review.html): Hostinger: Premium is $2.99/mo ($143.52 up front, 3 sites, 20 GB SSD) renewing at $10.99. The headline price only holds if you prepay years up front.
- [Joiin Review (2026): $23 for One Company, $92 for Ten](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/joiin-review.html): Joiin: 14-day free trial, no credit card; unlimited users and reports on every plan. The $23 headline covers a single company on annual billing.
- [Leavo Review (2026): From $2.49/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/leavo-review.html): Leavo: Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15). The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat.
- [Melio Review (2026): Free Tier, Then $25/mo](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/melio-review.html): Melio: A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. The free plan is genuinely useful for low bill 
- [Modge Review (2026): $4 a Seat, Screenshots Off by Default](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/modge-review.html): Modge: Basic is $5 per seat per month billed monthly or $4 billed annually. The numbers on Modge's own pages do not agree with each other.
- [Mycroft Review (2026): A Feature List With the Prices Removed](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/mycroft-review.html): Mycroft has no public pricing: three packages, and not one number between them. The pricing page is a feature list with the prices taken out.
- [Navan Review (2026): Free to 300 Staff, Expense $15 From User 6](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/navan-review.html): Navan Expense is free for the first 5 monthly expensing users and then $15 per user per month. 'Free' is real but has a mechanism.
- [Ngram Review (2026): 3,000 Credits Is Five Minutes](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/ngram-review.html): Ngram: Credit-based, three published tiers plus a quote-only Enterprise, with annual billing 20% off. Premium AI generation runs from 10 credits a sec
- [Niural AI Review (2026): $100 Platform Fee Plus $20 a Head](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/niural-ai-review.html): Niural AI: Eight products, each priced separately. The prices are published — which in payroll is genuinely rare and worth crediting.
- [Nouswise Review (2026): Two Prices on One Website](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/nouswise-review.html): Nouswise: Four tiers, billed monthly. Their own site does not agree with itself about what this costs, and we have now checked that twice.
- [Oyster Review (2026): Two Costs Have No Figure](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/oyster-review.html): Oyster: Employer of Record USD 699 per employee per month, with annual discounts available. The two numbers that decide your bill are not on the price
- [Proton Review (2026): From $3.99/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/proton-review.html): Proton: Free is $0.00 a month for 1 GB and one address. Storage is the axis, and the jump from Drive Plus to Unlimited is not really about storage at 
- [Proton Drive Review (2026): From $3.99/mo, Checked Aug 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/proton-drive-review.html): Proton Drive: Proton Duo is $14.99 for 2 TB across two users at $179.88 a year. End-to-end encryption is the point and the price.
- [QuickBooks UK Review (2026): The 90% Offer Ends at Month Six](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/quickbooks-uk-review.html): QuickBooks UK: Sole Trader Plus £10, Simple Start £16, Essentials £38 for three users, Plus £56 for five and Advanced £123 for twenty-five.
- [Remote People Review (2026): EOR From $199 an Employee a Month](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/remote-people-review.html): Remote People: US PEO from $99 per employee a month and US payroll from $29. The monthly rates are the cheapest we have on file for this category.
- [Rippling Review (2026): HR, IT and Finance, Priced by Quote](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/rippling-review.html): Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The published '$8 per user a month' is real but it's only the floor, and it's the HR-and-payroll entry.
- [Shoeboxed Review (2026): Two Plans Yearly, Two Monthly](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/shoeboxed-review.html): Shoeboxed: $0.30/$0.15/$0.10 per digital scan, $2.00 or $1.50 per paper scan, $9 per extra envelope. Built for businesses drowning in PAPER receipts.
- [TestGorilla Review (2026): Paid Tiers Are Annual Only](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/testgorilla-review.html): TestGorilla: Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat.
- [TextExpander Review (2026): macOS Already Does the Basics](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/textexpander-review.html): TextExpander: Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted.
- [Top Echelon Review (2026): From $79/mo, Checked Sep 2026](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/top-echelon-review.html): Top Echelon: $95 billed annually or $115 month-to-month on Professional. Almost everything people shop for sits in Professional, not Standard.
- [Tresorit Review (2026): From €16/user, No Server-Side Search](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/tresorit-review.html): Tresorit: €23.99, €16 and €20 on yearly. You pay the Swiss-E2EE premium — noticeably above mainstream clouds and above Proton Drive per GB.
- [World Businesses for Sale Review (2026): 3%, 2% or 1%](https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/world-businesses-for-sale-review.html): World Businesses for Sale: Browsing is free for buyers. On the broker plans you pay twice: a listing fee up front AND commission when it sells.
